target_customer: Airport travelers who rent cars, and local car owners who park them at the airport for free and earn rental income
problem: Airport car rentals are expensive and airport parking costs money. FlightCar let owners leave cars in its lot, rented them out to arriving visitors, and shared the income.
business_model: Peer to peer marketplace taking a share of rental revenue, with free parking and a car wash offered to owners
product_category: Peer to peer airport car rental

founders.name: Rujul Zaparde
prior_employers: Y Combinator (Visiting Partner, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is now Co-Founder and CEO at Zip.

founders.name: Kevin Petrovic
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. No background found.

founders.name: Shri Ganeshram
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder with Rujul Zaparde and Kevin Petrovic by TechCrunch (2013-04-15); not listed on the YC page.

exit.acquirer: Mercedes-Benz Research and Development North America (technology platform only)
exit.reason: Not stated in the announcement coverage opened

competitors.name: Traditional airport rental car companies
competitors.what: Counter based rental firms that FlightCar's founder said it competed with more than anything
competitors.traction_then: Incumbent operators at SFO, which required off-airport rivals to pay fees; San Francisco's city attorney sued FlightCar over this in June 2013

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace software plus physical operations: lots, shuttles, insurance coverage and vehicle handling at several airports. The operations were harder than the software.

defensibility.rationale: Airport locations and supply of owner cars built some local network effect, but the model depended on airport permission and insurance, and was copyable by rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents and airports fought it legally. SF's city attorney sued in June 2013, and the Millbrae location was ordered shut over code issues. The company later closed all 12 airport locations in July 2016 and sold its platform to Mercedes-Benz R&D North America.

market_need_then: Airport rental prices and parking fees were high, and the CS Monitor (2013-06) described owners getting free parking while earning money. Early press in 2013 covered launches at SFO and Boston.

branding.brand_signature: Free airport parking in exchange for renting out your car
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by CS Monitor, TechCrunch, Auto Rental News and others in 2013; backers included Brian Chesky per the YC description. No merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear descriptive name and a simple offer got broad press coverage, but no sourced mascot or community; the brand did not survive the 2016 shutdown.

outcome_analysis: FlightCar raised about $40.4 million through an April 2013 round, a $13.5 million Series A in September 2014 and a $20.7 million Series B in October 2015, expanding to 12 airports. A June 2013 San Francisco city attorney lawsuit and a Millbrae closure order show regulatory friction, and StrictlyVC described the 2015 raise as coming amid a major restructuring. It closed all locations in July 2016 and sold its technology to Mercedes-Benz R&D North America, but no company statement of cause was found, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: Website field was empty in the directory (company is shut down). The $5.5M April 2013 round is stage other because TechCrunch's headline gives no stage while StartupIntros calls it Series A; the 2013 seed of $590K from YC and SV Angel is reported by TechCrunch and its date is not given, so it is null. Later totals vary: about $40.4M (Skift, YC page), $41.1M to $46.8M on aggregators. A Sept 2014 article says $6.5M was raised before, consistent with $5.5M plus seed. Peer to peer rivals such as RelayRides were not found in a source dated near the batch, so only the traditional incumbents are listed. The shutdown reason is not given in the Auto Rental News piece. Audit fix: TechCrunch (2013-04-15) calls the 5.5M April 2013 round a Series A and names General Catalyst, SoftBank Capital, First Round Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Brian Chesky, Seacrest Global Group, Alexis Ohanian, Garry Tan, Harj Taggar, Emmett Shear and Erik Blachford, so the stage is series_a and the investors are updated. Because of that, the 2014-09 13.5M round is recorded as series_b and the 2015 20.7M round as series_c so the sequence is consistent, although contemporaneous outlets (PhocusWire, TechCrunch, PE International) call the 2014 round a Series A and StrictlyVC and Global Venturing call the 2015 round a Series B. The seed of 590K from Y Combinator and SV Angel was received before the February 2013 launch per TechCrunch; no exact date is given, so it is recorded as 2013 (an aggregator lists February 2013). Co-founder Shri Ganeshram is added per TechCrunch.
